extracted.intended_audience: researchers based at UK research organisations seeking EPSRC/UKRI funding
extracted.subtask_description: Information and requirements for applying to EPSRC (and multi-council UKRI) funding opportunities, including applicant eligibility, project scope, funding amounts, funder lists, and application windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host organisation eligibility (Centre for Quantum Commercialisation Skills)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must be based at a UK research organisation eligible for EPSRC funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit eligibility requirement for the Centre for Quantum Commercialisation Skills opportunity; applicants not based at eligible UK research organisations are not eligible to apply. No further detail on eligible organisation types is provided on this page (applicants should consult the full opportunity guidance for the definition of 'eligible').

rubrics_metrics.name: Project scope — Centre for Quantum Commercialisation Skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply for funding to establish a UK centre for quantum commercialisation skills that will provide opportunities for researchers to develop commercialisation skills, engage with industry, and explore new career pathways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the intended purpose and scope of the funded activity; proposals should align with establishing a centre focused on commercialisation skills, industry engagement and career pathways for researchers. Further scope/detail likely in the full opportunity text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award range and funding type — Centre for Quantum Commercialisation Skills
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the scale of funding available and that the mechanism is a grant. Applicants should plan budgets consistent with this award range and check detailed funding rules in the full call documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application window and timing — Centre for Quantum Commercialisation Skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Opening date: 6 May 2026 9:00am UK time. Closing date: 7 July 2026 4:00pm UK time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must be submitted within the stated opening and closing times. Applicants should ensure submission systems, institutional approvals and any required attachments are completed before the stated closing time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation-only requirement — UKRI metascience scientometrics for research assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: You must be invited to apply for this funding opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This opportunity is not open to general application; only invited applicants may submit. Prospective applicants should not prepare or submit unless they have been formally invited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding amount and cost basis — UKRI metascience scientometrics for research assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: We expect to fund up to ������������£3 million at 80% full economic cost (FEC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The expected total funding available and the cost basis (80% FEC) indicate how eligible project costs will be covered. Applicants should prepare budgets in line with 80% FEC rules and be aware of the total fund available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funders and co-funders (multi-council nature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Funders: UK Research and Innovation, Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC), Natural Environment Research Council (NERC), Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council (BBSRC), Arts and Humanities Research Council (AHRC), Science and Technology Facilities Council (STFC), Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC), Medical Research Council (MRC). Co-funders: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This opportunity is a multi-council (and government co-funded) activity; applicants should note the participating funders as this may affect remit, assessment criteria, and administrative arrangements. Check the full call text for funder-specific expectations or remit constraints.
